entries.notes: Max contribution period = 47 years (age 18-70). ~39 years at/above YMPE generally earns the maximum benefit.

entries.label: CPP base-component drop-out: years of lowest earnings excludable
entries.source_note: canada.ca 'How much you could receive' (CPP benefit amount page), fetched 2026-09-30.
entries.notes: Up to 8 years of lowest earnings excluded when calculating the CPP base component.

entries.label: CPP enhanced-component: best years of earnings used
entries.source_note: canada.ca 'How much you could receive' (CPP benefit amount page), fetched 2026-09-30.
entries.notes: Enhanced component uses your best 40 years of earnings.

entries.label: CPP child-rearing provision exists
entries.source_note: canada.ca 'How much you could receive' (CPP benefit amount page), fetched 2026-09-30.
entries.notes: Low/no earnings while looking after young children may be excluded, increasing the retirement pension and helping qualify for other benefits.

entries.label: CPP post-retirement contributions: mandatory stop age
entries.source_note: canada.ca 'How much you could receive' (CPP benefit amount page), fetched 2026-09-30.
entries.notes: While receiving CPP and under 70, contributions are mandatory if working (each year buys a post-retirement benefit). May elect to stop at 65; contributions stop at 70 regardless.

entries.label: No CPP timing benefit past age 70
entries.source_note: canada.ca 'When to start your retirement pension', confirmed 2026-09-30.
entries.notes: Maximum monthly amount is reached at 70; waiting longer gains nothing.

entries.label: Combined CPP retirement + survivor's pension: cap rule
entries.value: capped at the maximum CPP retirement pension
entries.source_note: Service Canada publication 'The Canada Pension Plan Retirement Pension' (official): 'The most you can receive if eligible for both the CPP retirement pension and the CPP survivor's pension is the maximum retirement pension'; 'you cannot receive a maximum survivor's pension while also receiving a maximum CPP retirement pension'. Corroborated by ESDC quarterly report Jul-Sep 2026 (combined survivor/retirement max $1,531.56). Confirmed via search 2026-09-30.
entries.notes: Deferring your own CPP to 70 for +42% can buy less than it appears when a survivor pension will also be in play; the tool flags this and does not compute survivor dollars.

entries.label: Maximum CPP survivor's pension, survivor 65+ (Jan 2026)
entries.source_note: ESDC 'Maximum Benefit Amounts and Related Figures: CPP (2026) and OAS (July to September 2026)' quarterly report, via search 2026-09-30.
entries.notes: Survivor under 65 max: $803.54/mo (flat $238.17 + earnings-related $565.37).
